sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Pooja Logistics is a real, growing cold-chain carrier, but not yet a demonstrated capital-light compounder. At the authenticated 19 October 2026 close of ₹125.05, market capitalization is ₹178.62 crore. Business Quality is 5.02 /10 (5.0 displayed), Growth Quality is 5.60 /10 (5.6 displayed), and Investment Attractiveness remains NS because the ordinary expected-return factor cannot be established without assuming replacement financing. The appropriate action is a financing-sensitive watchlist, not an actionable buy price.

Three details change the apparent bargain. First, reported FY26 EPS ₹12.00 predates the full IPO share count; attributable earnings rebased to current shares are only about ₹8.64. Second, the IPO buys 92 vehicles, but 49 replace vehicles nearing practical retirement; only 43 are net expansion before other disposals. Third, ₹9.33 crore of new lien-restricted deposits sits inside reported operating cash flow. The weak FY26 CFO figure therefore cannot be interpreted as pure operating burn, but these deposits are not free cash either.

The base cash bridge supports the initial plan through March 2027, so there is no evidenced funding failure. Beyond that, continuing fleet renewal and expansion require financing. Conditional 65% asset finance at 10.5% produces roughly 14.9% annualized return at 8 x terminal EBITDA; the equity-rescue alternative produces only 12.6%. Neither is an ordinary expected return. The main thesis-break variable is the cash yield after replacement capex, customer collection and financing, not reported EBITDA alone.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 6, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 5, BAL 4, EXEC 6, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 4 and L NS. Each has material evidence, a contrary fact and confidence; the detailed factor audit follows. No factor is replaced with a neutral 5 because it is unknown. BQS=5.02; GQS=5.60. IAS uses the unrounded BQS, so the Q contribution is 1.255 rather than 1.25.

BQS weights are GOV 20%, MOAT 20%, REV 12%, DUR 10%, CAP 12%, CASH 10%, BAL 8%, EXEC 8%. GQS weights are REV 40%, DUR 20%, EARN 15%, CAP 15%, CASH 10%. IAS weights are Q25%, R35%, D 20%, P 10%, L 10%. Missing R and L leave 55% IAS coverage and known contribution 2.255. Diagnostic bounds are 2.705–6.755, not an estimated score. Raw and final aggregates are identical where computable; there is no undisclosed risk haircut.

The persistent-weak-cash growth ceiling is explicitly evaluated and not triggered. CASH 5 reflects mixed realization, not persistent<=3 evidence: the three-year adjusted after-interest ratio is 1.006 x. CAP 5 reflects mixed periods rather than demonstrated persistent destruction. sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company transports temperature-sensitive goods in refrigerated trucks for food, dairy, confectionery, QSR and related customers. Customers purchase reliable temperature-controlled delivery, vehicle availability and route execution. The company earns transport revenue, pays fuel, drivers, repairs, toll/documentation and hired-vehicle charges, then waits for customers to settle invoices. It generally operates trip-to-trip rather than from a guaranteed backlog. Freight activity, not the small historic securities-trading line, is the core business.

The FY26 fleet consists of 424 owned vehicles. Internally attributed owned-vehicle revenue was ₹112.07 crore, about 67.63% of total; hired-vehicle revenue ₹53.63 crore, about 32.37%. The hired fleet is variable, and its vehicle count is not disclosed as a stable capacity number. It is not equivalent to owned productive capacity or a capitalized finance lease. Vehicle loans fund owned assets; hired-truck and office-rent charges remain operating cash expenses. The model follows that cash-rent convention throughout.

Truckit India is a 99.996%-owned subsidiary acquired during FY24. The group FY24 income statement includes only four months of that subsidiary, whereas the parent has a full financial year. The prospectus narrative occasionally says the consolidated period is four months; this must not be read as only four months of the entire parent's trading. The model values consolidated operating earnings and includes the immaterial minority claim. No extra value is added for operating assets already supporting earnings.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Cold-chain reliability has economic value: cargo spoilage, missed delivery windows and vehicle breakdowns can be costly to customers. A trained driver/vendor network, maintenance systems, GPS and temperature monitoring create useful operating know-how. Mechanism: reliable execution earns repeat business. Evidence: longstanding customer relationships, rising revenue and a 424-vehicle fleet. Durability: moderate if standards and vehicle condition are maintained. Failure mode: an equally capable rival, customer procurement pressure or deteriorating service can replace the relationship.

There is insufficient evidence of a structural moat. The largest FY26 customer contributed 27.69%, the top 10 contributed 68.15%, and 95.07% of revenue came from FMCG. Top 10 concentration improved from 81.61% in FY24, a real positive, but a few buyers still influence rates and service requirements. Customers prefer owned vehicles in some cases, which creates a retention incentive to invest rather than necessarily a pricing premium. Trip-level work and hired-fleet substitution limit contractual protection.

No market-share rank is asserted: a dated, like-for-like denominator for the reachable refrigerated-road-transport niche was not established. Large national cold-chain TAM figures would not prove accessible demand or cash returns for this company. Snowman, broader logistics carriers and local reefer operators are relevant economic alternatives, but unverified peer multiples are not used as valuation evidence. A capable competitor must invest in trucks, maintenance and relationships, but there is no demonstrated exclusive technology or network barrier that prevents it.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The preselected long window is parent freight activity, not the most flattering consolidated CAGR. FY21 freight revenue ₹62.86 crore grew to FY26 parent revenue ₹149.23 crore, about 18.9% over five intervals. Reported parent revenue including the earlier goods line grew from ₹64.00 crore to ₹149.23 crore. FY23 transport revenue ₹110.58 crore to FY26 ₹149.23 crore gives approximately 10.5% over three intervals. The six observations and each annual ₹addition are retained, so a five-year CAGR is not incorrectly calculated from five observations.

For the latest common group perimeter, FY25 revenue ₹148.77 crore increased to FY26 ₹165.70 crore, +11.38% and ₹16.93 crore. The FY24–26 group CAGR is shown only as a reported scope-changing statistic: the first year contains partial subsidiary contribution. The parent-only bridge removes the acquisition-investment balance for capital analysis, but parent sales are not claimed to be perfectly third-party organic group sales because intercompany activity is not fully separated.

The growth mix is not simply 92 more trucks. Owned revenue increased ₹13.29 crore in FY26, hired revenue about ₹3.71 crore; the owned fleet rose 60 units. Revenue per ending owned vehicle fell from about ₹27.14 lakh to ₹26.43 lakh, while an average-fleet proxy is higher. Commissioning timing and mix may explain this, so the decline is not automatically poor utilization. Existing-customer business represented 95.01% of FY26 revenue, with new customers ₹8.27 crore. No price-versus-trip-volume bridge or current-quarter trajectory was disclosed. REV starts at 7 on the five-year anchor and receives net-1 for the pandemic starting-year distortion and sustained lower recent growth, not for small company size.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The IPO quotes 92 new reefers for ₹33.9739 crore before GST, approximately ₹36.93 lakh each. Forty-nine existing vehicles are expected to reach practical replacement age within the next year. The plan therefore has only 43 net additions before further disposals. The initial purchase plan has no placed orders at the prospectus date, is scheduled through FY27, and its cost may rise for tax, freight or specification changes. These are funded intentions, not commissioned earnings.

The operating model begins with 424 owned vehicles and conservatively phases the 92 purchases during January–March 2027. Later replacement counts are the ceiling of the opening fleet divided by a nine-year useful operating life; expansion is separately 20 net vehicles annually in the base case. This sits within management's 8–10 year practical life rather than treating six-year WDV depreciation as maintenance cash cost. Quoted cost inflates 5% annually and an analyst 18% nonrecoverable-tax allowance is tested at 0% and 28%. These allowances are not legal conclusions about the applicable tax rate. Hired revenue fills demand beyond owned-fleet capacity, so revenue cannot be double-counted as both insourced existing work and new demand.

Parent incremental NOPAT/capital is 22.73% over FY23–26,14.04% over FY24–26 and 4.83% in FY26 alone. Group latest-year proxy is 4.68%, or 6.47% when new restricted deposits are excluded from capital. These are accounting diagnostics, not cohort IRRs: old-margin recovery, WDV ageing and young capital timing matter. CWIP ₹4.503 crore remains committed capital and is not paid again in the forward cash bridge. The bottom-up model indicates a real runway, but continued capex is not self-financing in the no-new-lending base case. Growth quality is mixed, not disproved by low reported CFO alone.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters and their group retain approximately 68.45% after the fresh IPO versus 93.68% before it. The IPO has no selling-shareholder OFS, so cash is intended for the business. Pre IPO shareholders lose 26.93% of their proportional ownership from the IPO issuance; the earlier 4.38 lakh-share placement raised ₹4.1172 crore at ₹94, compared with ₹115 in the IPO. The 99:1 bonus in 2024 changes share units but is not economic dilution. No live zero-pledge guarantee is inferred from pre-issue disclosure.

Disclosed FY26 director remuneration is ₹0.975 crore, family rent ₹0.1632 crore and an additional disclosed family salary ₹0.315 crore. Commercial related-party dealings are not, on their own, minority abuse. The relevant tests are pricing, necessity, cash settlement and whether proceeds migrate into related entities. Statutory auditors changed from Singhal Garg to Maroti in FY25; CARO says outgoing auditor communications were considered. No record of an information-denial resignation was found. Restatement work by Singhal Garg is a different engagement, not a second current statutory opinion.

Observable execution is mixed-positive. The fleet rose 364→424; the company implemented its December 2024 driver-contracting change; it completed a fresh equity issue. But payroll decline is offset by ₹10.34 crore contractual-driver expense and ₹3.92 crore advances, so cost migration is not automatically productivity. The 92-vehicle IPO commitment remains to be verified through registrations, invoices, funding and customer deployment. The dated promises-versus-delivery register is embedded; absence of promotional guidance is not penalized.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The historical panel preserves scope and restatement labels. Consolidated FY24/FY25/FY26 revenue is ₹123.75/148.77/165.70 crore; operating EBITDA ₹19.13/23.09/27.30 crore; PAT ₹5.73/11.02/12.34 crore. FY25 original PAT ₹10.44 crore becomes ₹11.02 crore after gratuity/tax restatement. FY24 original PAT ₹6.03 crore becomes ₹5.73 crore. FY23 parent original and restated profits also differ. The current earnings calculation uses the latest restatement, not whichever version looks stronger.

Reported three-year CFO is ₹30.1976 crore against PAT ₹29.0935 crore, 1.038 x. Reported cash capex totals ₹38.0710 crore, leaving FCF proxy-₹7.8734 crore before financing-classified interest. FY26 CFO ₹3.1913 crore contains ₹9.3253 crore of new lien FDs inside other current assets. Remove that investment-like absorption, remove the ₹1.0116 crore release of vehicle advances, remove ₹1.5079 crore investment gains, and correct net disposal losses: diagnostic CFO becomes ₹10.0434 crore before interest, ₹7.1388 crore after interest. The same method across three years gives ₹29.2678 crore, 1.006 x PAT. This does not create spendable restricted cash; it distinguishes operating realization from allocation to pledged deposits.

Receivables rose ₹7.47 crore in FY26, faster than sales, while ending-day proxy increases from 56.29 to 67.00 days. Driver advances are new and their settlement ageing is not disclosed. Most trade receivables are younger than six months; a small ₹0.0276 crore disputed item exceeds three years and appears doubtful in ageing with no main-table allowance. Cash at March 2026 is ₹4.1094 crore, dominated by ₹3.5784 crore physical cash; the prior-year cash figure included ₹5.0487 crore cheques in hand. These deserve collection and custody follow-up without an unsupported fraud assertion.

Full FY25/FY26 main audit, IFC, CARO and audit-trail annexures are unmodified, with bank returns agreeing to books, no reported default and an operating/preserved edit trail. This is narrower than a guarantee. A derived original FY26 standalone cash reconciliation moves ₹3.6792 crore share premium from operating to financing cash: original CFF ₹7.8094 crore becomes ₹11.4886 crore, equal to the latest consolidated CFF; original CFO ₹6.8059 crore becomes ₹3.1267 crore, leaving ₹0.0646 crore group difference. This exact arithmetic supports a classification explanation but is not a new auditor opinion. Original standalone cash presentations and an early FY21 comparative cash mismatch are retained as limitations; they are not pooled with consolidated PAT. The source-safe capital reconciliation includes goodwill once, deferred tax exclusions, tiny NCI, restricted capital and source-rounding residuals. The model settles current statutory and interest dues once; opening TDS credits offset the old income-tax provision, with no speculative refund. Borrowings, restricted deposits and IPO earmarks are kept distinct.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹125.05 and 14.284 million shares, equity value is ₹178.62142 crore. Reported FY26 P/E is approximately 14.48 x on current issued shares, not 10.42 x using historical EPS12.00. Deducting other income at 25% normalized tax gives PAT about ₹10.79 crore and P/E about 16.56 x. Historical March net debt, excluding lien FDs, is ₹27.13 crore. The post-IPO proforma EV diagnostic must reserve ₹33.9739 crore for fleet use; deducting all IPO cash while assuming the new fleet's earnings would double-count capital.

Primary valuation is a linked fleet model with terminal EV/EBITDA, not a bare peer multiple. The method is usable only because replacement capex, working capital, debt service, cash reserves and ownership dilution are explicitly charged before terminal equity. Bear/base/bull exit assumptions are 5 x/8 x/10 x. As a cross-check, FY26 cash before new working capital and replacement capex is only about ₹20.83 crore after normalized tax and interest. Replacing 49 trucks at the average quote costsabout ₹18.09 crore before tax or ₹21.35 crore with the 18% allowance. That leaves approximately ₹2.73 crore to-₹0.52 crore before working-capital growth, far below accounting PAT. This is a maintenance estimate, not a disclosed free-cash-flow line.

Intraperiod checks place fixed obligations before collections, and a separate 15-day operating-cost lag plus cash payment of the opening ₹4.0046 crore tax provision tests temporary settlement risk. Rescue is prefunded before the worst modeled interval point, not inserted after a deficit. Unfinanced base and bull paths breach the chosen ₹3 crore cash reserve during the projection; their nonrescue returns and entry prices are null even where terminal equity appears positive. The base with 65% future vehicle debt at 10.5% is funded and returns about 14.9%; it ends with ₹65.74 crore debt. Adding full OD-lien release raises conditional return to about 15.5%. Base explicit equity rescue requires about ₹32.37 crore net and produces 12.6%; fully stressed rescue requires ₹74.76 crore net and produces-13.3%. These assumptions are not current commitments or ordinary expected returns.

Reverse solves use funded finite brackets and residual tests. In the base rescue case, a 15% hurdle requires about 8.88 x terminal EBITDA or 15.84% annual demand growth. Entry-price sensitivities at 12%/15%/18% re-solve price-dependent rescue dilution; the approximate ₹129.54/109.63/92.62 outputs are analytical thresholds, not actionable buy ranges. Complete monthly cash, annual models and 72 two-way sensitivities and nine reverse solutions are embedded, including reserve, physical-cash, tax-cost, collection, lending and litigation assumptions.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest contrary case is that the IPO mainly renews an ageing fleet, while the largest customers keep bargaining power and contracted drivers absorb cash. A revenue slowdown can coexist with higher fleet replacement cost, larger receivables, bank-facility expiry and an adverse tax outcome. In this chain, EBITDA remains positive but fails to pay replacement capex, existing principal and rising working capital. Assets may be productive yet equity holders suffer from emergency lending or discounted issuance.

The unfunded bear variant assumes only the ₹13.4608 crore disputed tax principal; the severe funded bear below instead pays the full ₹27.0084 crore claim including penalty, interest and fees. Those variants are not an identical-operating-case before/after-financing comparison. The severe modeled path combines 2% annual demand growth, 17% owned and 5% hired EBITDA margins, 90-day receivables, 28% vehicle-tax allowance and full ₹27.0084 crore disputed GST cash settlement. It does not call the claim legally certain. Without financing, liquidity fails; explicit rescue prefunds each interval and issues whole shares at 25% discount with 3% fees. Net rescue ₹74.76 crore dilutes owners sufficiently that terminal share value isabout ₹61.22, approximately 51% below the reference price. Disposed vehicles receive modest salvage, no extra property value is added, and terminal cash keeps the operating reserve.

The alternative is favorable: demand remains healthy, loans roll on acceptable asset-backed terms, customer advances settle, vehicles arrive on budget, and the GST appeal succeeds. The additional 15-day cash-collection lag and full opening-tax-payment scenario fails even before the cutoff if unfinanced; its funded counterfactual requires ₹47.85 crore rescue and returns about 11.22%. A hypothetical pre-entry rescue changes the modeled entry share count and is not evidence that such an issuance or actual deficit occurred. The purpose of the bear model is to identify the necessary evidence and the mechanism of permanent loss, not to assign a false probability. A reserve-floor breach is an analyst scenario, not an actual default. The thesis fails as a compounder thesis if post-replacement cash returns stay below the operating capital hurdle even while revenue and accounting EPS rise.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold share-price outcomes over the exact five-year horizon require approximately 38% and 58% annualized shareholder returns. Multiplying current EPS by an arbitrary future P/E is insufficient because shares, debt and replacement spending change. The embedded test keeps the base rescue dilution, solves required terminal equity and EBITDA at 8 x, translates to revenue at 19% blended margin and then to owned-vehicle equivalents at FY26 average yield.

The result is a scale requirement, not a forecast. It would demand much more customer demand and fleet funding than the 92 gross vehicle plan, while hired fleets have thinner economics and customers remain concentrated. Further funding beyond the base path would dilute equity or raise debt and increase the required operating outcome. A reliable reachable-market denominator and verified unit returns are unavailable, so no probability or market-share claim is assigned. Current evidence supports testing whether growth can be funded at acceptable per-share returns before treating 5×or 10×as an investable thesis.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Monitor specific evidence rather than only the next profit headline:
1. By March 2027, reconcile 92 invoices/registrations, 49 replacement disposals, net additions and actual all-in cost against ₹33.9739 crore ex-tax; flag cost overrun above 10% or late commissioning.
2. Obtain the post-IPO proceeds ledger:₹33.9739 crore fleet allocation, ₹4.691 crore GCP, ₹5.5641 crore estimated issue cost and any extra tax. No double use of earmarked cash.
3. At 30 November 2026, establish OD renewal or repayment, actual borrowing headroom and lien FD release terms; do not count a sanction limit as undrawn cash.
4. Receivable ending days baseline 67.0; investigate sustained above 80 days, rising older-than-one year balances, and the small disputed item without allowance.
5. Contract-driver advances baseline ₹3.9212 crore: require settlement-ageing, recoverability and cash collection evidence. Payroll reduction alone is not a success metric.
6. Compare operating cash after classification normalization and interest with PAT; warn if a rolling comparable three-year ratio fallsbelow 0.8 x or deficits persist after deposit movements are separated.
7. Track owned-versus-hired share, revenue per average vehicle, service claims and top customer exposure 27.69%; loss of a major route without cost flexibility is a thesis warning.
8. Follow GST orders/appeals and required cash deposits, plus the October 2026 civil/work-injury hearings; distinguish management confidence from adjudicated outcome.
9. Verify replacement finance rate, tenure, principal schedule and loan-to-cost rather than assuming 65% at 10.5%; monitor cash after fleet renewal and a ₹3 crore illustrative reserve.
10. Recheck liquidity after 60 actual listed sessions, with spreads and depth; compare a whole-lot position with conservative turnover participation, not IPO-day averages.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: Watchlist — financing-sensitive; Investment Attractiveness unscored. BQS5.0 and GQS5.6 describe a business with established operations and a real growth opportunity, but only mixed evidence of durable returns and cash generation after replacement. The company does not pass a high-confidence compounder standard. No governance Avoid override or evidenced funding Fail is asserted.

There is no ordinary entry-price range at this stage. A cheaper quoted P/E does not solve a funding shortfall, and a higher terminal multiple does not make an unfunded path investable. The analytical rescue/debt prices in the model are conditional outputs, not recommendations. A favorable reclassification would require verified delivery, cost-inclusive capex, repeatable collections, sustainable replacement-financing commitments and resolution or financeable containment of the tax exposure. A seasoned liquidity record is also necessary for a practical new position.

A lower price can improve prospective return only within a demonstrably funded model and at realistic dilution. Business-quality rankings remain separate from price-sensitive attractiveness. This is general research using public information and explicit assumptions, not personalized financial advice or a solicitation to trade.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary hierarchy: dated NSE security master and actual bhavcopies establish identity, capital and reference price; final issuer-hosted prospectus establishes current IPO terms and latest restated group accounts; full issuer annual reports establish statutory audit and annexure findings; older exchange DRHP and audited statements establish parent history. Website fleet headlines and secondary IPO summaries do not override dated primary filings. Every retained source has a title, URL, publication/retrieval date, locator and original-byte hash where downloaded. Source-safe extracts preserve facts, not original PDFs, OCR, personal identifiers or shareholder lists.

The chief assumptions are demand 12%, owned/hired EBITDA margins 21.5%/8%, 20 net new vehicles annually after FY27, nine-year physical replacement, five-percent cost inflation, an 18% vehicle/issue-tax allowance, 67-day receivables, ₹3 crore cash reserve and 8 x terminal EBITDA. The unfinanced case assumes no new loan commitments and no lien release; separate funded alternatives add 65% asset finance or explicit discounted equity rescue. Actual schedules, tax recoverability and private bank balances are not asserted. The absence of private daily bank data alone does not create a funding Hold; the cash model, known IPO and obligations determine the conditional gate.

Open questions that could change the verdict: which driver advances settled after March; how the original standalone cash presentations reconcile to the latest restatement; whether lien FDs can be released after OD repayment; actual truck andissue costs including tax; committed future vehicle-finance terms; acquisition-adjusted third-party revenue; outcomes of October hearings; current promoter pledges; and realized per-vehicle cash return from the new fleet. Unavailable TTM, exact organic group CAGR and market share remain ND. A reconstruction reproduces retained inputs and arithmetic, not fresh authentication of source files that are no longer present.

summary:
Pooja Logistics is a real, growing cold-chain carrier, but not yet a demonstrated capital-light compounder. At the authenticated 19 October 2026 close of ₹125.05, market capitalization is ₹178.62 crore. Business Quality is 5.02 /10 (5.0 displayed), Growth Quality is 5.60 /10 (5.6 displayed), and Investment Attractiveness remains NS because the ordinary expected-return factor cannot be established without assuming replacement financing. The appropriate action is a financing-sensitive watchlist, not an actionable buy price.

Three details change the apparent bargain. First, reported FY26 EPS ₹12.00 predates the full IPO share count; attributable earnings rebased to current shares are only about ₹8.64. Second, the IPO buys 92 vehicles, but 49 replace vehicles nearing practical retirement; only 43 are net expansion before other disposals. Third, ₹9.33 crore of new lien-restricted deposits sits inside reported operating cash flow. The weak FY26 CFO figure therefore cannot be interpreted as pure operating burn, but these deposits are not free cash either.

The base cash bridge supports the initial plan through March 2027, so there is no evidenced funding failure. Beyond that, continuing fleet renewal and expansion require financing. Conditional 65% asset finance at 10.5% produces roughly 14.9% annualized return at 8 x terminal EBITDA; the equity-rescue alternative produces only 12.6%. Neither is an ordinary expected return. The main thesis-break variable is the cash yield after replacement capex, customer collection and financing, not reported EBITDA alone.
